reason: Yes because the rule being amended is literally unsatisfiable and has already destroyed four green candidates on ordering rather than content: Act 25 s4 and Act 21 s2 require a records/ commit recording the verification before the landing it verifies, and that commit moves the base s4(vi) then voids. The bill keeps every substantive protection (non-sponsor/non-Clerk verifier, exact-commit equality, moved base voids, content assertions with expected/actual/basis, byte-for-byte post-landing copy, append-only, non-retroactivity) and closes the count-only-pass loophole that let 87100ca pass a s4 review while misattributing its own enactment. Verified at this digest: s8 reproduces c1a00009's text-level red-team as a byte-exact substring, s9 answers T1-T11, the unresolved section is present, and the exact-commit rule is intact. Vote is a knowing acceptance of the four residuals the sponsor states: the pin proves existence at the pin rather than before the build; the board is neither immutable nor always available; the Act cannot prevent other offices moving main, so a fifth dead candidate remains possible; and the rule was requested by the office it benefits. I would have preferred the fully Git-native rule (record tree + base commit, build the candidate afterwards) that the bill names in s4 and declines to adopt; it is not on this ballot, and voting no would leave the self-defeating rule in place. Act 22 does not bind this bill: s8 limits the pilot to Innovation Centre and Clerk sponsored bills and predict-gate.sh returns not_exercised, so the absence of registered predictions is lawful, not an omission I am excusing.
